no sound of trees beneath the winds; but all things together
it shall melt down into one and refine into what is pure.
And when the imperishable angels of the immortal God,
Barakiel, Ramiel, Uriel, Samiel, and Azael,
knowing themselves whatever evil anyone did before,
shall bring the souls of men from the murky gloom,
all to judgment before the tribunal of God,
the immortal, the great; for he alone is imperishable,
the Almighty himself, who shall be the judge of mortals.
And then to the underworld dwellers souls and breath and speech
the Heavenly One will give, and bones fitted together
with all kinds of joints, flesh and sinews...
and veins, and skin around the flesh, and former hair
divinely compacted; and breathing, set in motion,
the bodies of earth-born mortals shall arise in one day.
And then, having shattered the monstrous bolts
and gates of relentless and unbreakable adamant
of unworked Hades, Uriel the great angel shall straightway cast them down,
and he shall bring all the much-mourning forms to judgment,
the phantoms especially of the ancient Titans
and of the Giants, and all whom the Flood overwhelmed,
and those whom the wave of the sea destroyed in the deeps,
and as many as wild beasts and reptiles and winged birds
feasted upon, all these he shall summon to the tribunal;
and again, those whom flesh-devouring fire destroyed in the flame,
these too he will gather and set before the tribunal of God.
And when he raises the dead, having abolished fate,
and Sabaoth Adonai, high-thundering, sits
upon his heavenly throne and sets up the great pillar,
then he himself, the imperishable one, shall come in a cloud to the Imperishable One,
Christ in glory with the blameless angels,
and he shall sit at the right hand of the Great One, judging at the tribunal
the life of the pious and the way of impious men.
Moses too shall come, the great friend of the Most High,
having put on flesh; and great Abraham himself shall come,
Isaac and Jacob, Joshua and Daniel and Elijah,
Habakkuk and Jonah and those whom the Hebrews killed.
And after Jeremiah, he will destroy them all at the judgment seat,
the Hebrews being judged, so that they might receive deeds worthy of their actions
and pay for whatever each one did in mortal life.
And then indeed all will pass through the burning river
and unquenchable flame; and the righteous
will all be saved, but the ungodly thereupon will perish
unto all ages—as many as previously wrought evil,
and committed murders, and as many as are accomplices,
liars and thieves, treacherous and dreadful wreckers of households,
parasites and adulterers, pouring forth abusive speech,
terrible, violent, lawless, and idolaters;
and as many as abandoned the great immortal God
and became blasphemers and plunderers of the pious,
destroyers of faith and murderers of righteous men;
and as many as with deceitful and shameless double faces,
elders and revered deacons look on...
showing partiality, they judge unjustly, acting for the favor of others,
persuaded by deceitfully false reports...
more destructive and more vile than panthers and wolves;
and as many as are exceedingly haughty and usurers,
who, piling up interest upon interest in their houses,
harm orphans and widows in every way;
and as many as give to widows and orphans
from unjust works, and as many as, giving from their own labors,
reproach them; and as many as in old age abandoned their parents,
not honoring them at all, nor giving back to their parents the cost of their nurture,
and moreover as many as were disobedient
and even spoke a harsh word against their begetters;
and as many as, having received pledges, denied them;
and servants who turned against their masters,
and again, those who defiled their flesh in licentiousness,
and as many as loosed the maidenly girdle
in secret intercourse, and as many women as cast out the burdens in their womb
by abortion, and as many as unlawfully expose their offspring;
sorcerers and sorceresses together with them, even these
the wrath of the heavenly and incorruptible God
will bring near to the pillar, where all around in a circle
a tireless fiery river flows; and all of them together
the angels of the immortal and ever-existing God,
with fiery whips and with chains of fire,
binding tightly from above with unbreakable bonds,
will punish most dreadfully; and then in the blackness of night
in Gehenna they will cast them beneath Tartarean beasts,
many and terrible, where there is boundless darkness.
And when they have inflicted many punishments
upon all whose heart was evil, then afterward again
a fiery wheel from the great river will encircle
them, because they cared for reckless deeds.
And then they will lament from afar, one here, another there,
with a most pitiful fate, fathers and infant children,
mothers and weeping children at the breast.
Nor will they have enough of tears, nor indeed will any voice
of those bitterly lamenting be heard from one to another,
but far under gloomy, moldering Tartarus
they will cry out in torment; and in unholy places
they will repay threefold for whatever evil deed they committed,
burning in much fire; and all will gnash their teeth,
wasting away with raging thirst and violence,
and they will call death noble, but it will flee from them.
For no longer will death, nor night, give them rest.
And they will make many pleas in vain to the high-ruling God,
and then he will openly turn his face away from them.
For he gave the days of seven ages for repentance
to wandering mortals through the hand of a pure virgin.
But the others, as many as care for justice and noble deeds,
and piety and most righteous thoughts,
angels, lifting them up through the burning river,
will lead into light and into a carefree life,
where is the immortal path of the great God
and three springs of wine and honey and milk.
And the earth, belonging equally to all, not divided by walls or fences,
will then yield more abundant fruits
of its own accord, and there will be shared livelihoods and undivided wealth.
For there will be no poor man there, nor rich, nor tyrant,
nor slave, nor again will anyone be great or small,
no kings, no leaders; but all will be together in common.
And no one will say at all, “Night has come,” nor indeed “Tomorrow,”
nor “Yesterday has happened,” nor will anyone worry about many days,
nor spring, nor summer, nor winter, nor autumn,
nor marriage, nor death, nor sales, nor purchases,
nor sunset, nor sunrise; for he will make one long day.
To these also the Almighty, imperishable God will grant another thing:
to the pious, whenever they make request of the imperishable God,
from the fierce fire and from the immortal gnashings
he will grant to save people; and this he will do.
For having gathered them again from the unwearied flame
and set them elsewhere, he will send them for the sake of his people
into another, eternal life for immortals
in the Elysian Plain, where are the long billows
of the ever-flowing, deep-bosomed Acherusian lake.
Alas for me, wretched one! What will become of me on that day,
because I, foolish one, having done wickedness in all things,
sinned, caring neither for marriage nor for prudent thoughts;
but even in the halls of my wealthy husband
I shut out the needy; and lawless deeds formerly I committed
knowingly. But you, Savior, from my scourgers
deliver me, brazen-faced though I am, who have done shameless things.
And I here beseech you, grant me a brief pause from my song,
holy Giver of manna, King of the great kingdom.
From the second discourse concerning God.
High-thundering, blessed, heavenly one, who has the Cherubim
as your seat, I beseech you, since I have spoken absolute truth,
give me a brief rest, for the heart within me is weary.
Yet why does my heart throb again, and why is my spirit,
struck by a whip, compelled from within to proclaim
a message to all? But again I will declare everything,
whatever God commands me to declare to humankind.
O human beings, who have a form fashioned by God in his image,
why do you wander in vain and not walk the straight path,
ever mindful of the immortal Creator?
There is one God, sole ruler, ineffable, dwelling in the ether,
self-begotten, invisible, yet seeing all things himself;
whom no stone-carver’s hand has made, nor by human crafts
is his form displayed from gold or ivory;
but he himself, the Eternal, revealed himself,
who is, and who was before, and likewise shall be hereafter.
For what mortal is able to behold God with eyes?
Or who can endure even to hear the name alone
of the great heavenly God who rules the cosmos?
He who created all things by his word: heaven and sea,
the unwearying sun and the full moon,
the shining stars, and mighty mother Tethys,
springs and rivers, imperishable fire, days and nights.
He indeed is God, who fashioned four-lettered Adam,
the first one formed, whose name completes
the east and west, the south and north;
and he established the form of the likeness of mortal humans,
and made wild beasts, creeping things, and winged birds.
You do not revere nor fear God, but wander in vain,
worshiping serpents and sacrificing to cats,
and to mute idols and stone statues of human beings;
and sitting before the doors of godless temples
you keep watch, [ignoring] the existing God, who preserves all things,
delighting in the wickedness of stones, forgetting the judgment
of the immortal Savior, who created heaven and earth.
Woe, bloodthirsty, treacherous, and evil race of the ungodly,
of false, double-tongued, and malicious men,
adulterers, idolaters, devising deceitful things,
in whose breasts is evil, in whom is a frenzied frenzy,
plundering for themselves, possessing a shameless spirit;
for no one who is rich and possesses wealth will share with another,
but terrible wickedness will be upon all mortals,
and they will have no faithfulness at all; and many widowed women
will secretly love other men for the sake of gain,
not keeping the bond of life, though having obtained husbands.
But when Rome shall also rule over Egypt,
though still delaying, then indeed the greatest kingdom
of the immortal King will appear over humankind.
And a holy ruler will come to hold the scepters of the whole earth
unto all ages as time hastens on.
And then the inexorable wrath of Latin men;
three will ruin Rome with a pitiable fate.
And all mortals will perish in their own homes,
whenever a fiery cataract pours down from heaven.
Alas for me, wretched one, when will that day come,
and the judgment of the immortal God, the great King?
Yet even now be built, O cities, and be adorned, all of you,
with temples and stadiums, market places and golden images,
and silver and stone ones, that you may come to the bitter day.
For it will come, whenever the smell of sulfur passes
among all humanity. But I will declare each thing,
in how many cities mortal humans bear wickedness.
And from the Sebastenes Beliar will come hereafter,
and he will raise up the height of the mountains, and he will raise up the sea,
the great fiery sun and the shining moon,
and he will raise up the dead and perform many signs
for mortals; but they will not be brought to fulfillment in him,
rather, he deceives mortals, and will deceive many,
both faithful and chosen Hebrews, and lawless men and other
people, who have not yet heard the word of God.
But whenever the threats of the great God draw near,
and a flaming power comes through the surging sea to the earth,
it will also burn up Beliar and the arrogant people,
all who put their trust in him.
And then indeed the world will be ruled under the hands
of a woman and obey in everything.
Then whenever a widow reigns over the whole world,
and casts gold and silver into the divine sea,
and casts the bronze and iron of ephemeral mortals
into the ocean, then indeed all the elements
of the world will be widowed, whenever God dwelling in the aether
rolls up heaven, just as a scroll is rolled up;
and the whole multiform vault of heaven will fall upon the divine earth
and the sea; and an unwearied cataract of raging fire
will pour down, and it will burn the earth, and burn the sea,
and the heavenly vault, and the days, and creation itself
it will melt into one and sift out into what is pure.
And no longer will there be the exultant spheres of the luminaries,
no night, no dawn, nor many days of care,
no spring, no summer, no winter, no autumn.
And then indeed the judgment of the great God will come into the midst
of the great age, when all these things come to pass.
Woe, woe for navigable waters and all the dry land!
When the sun rises, which indeed does not set again,
all things will obey him as he enters into the world again;
therefore indeed he first recognized him and his power.
But whenever the threats of the great God are fulfilled,
which he once threatened against mortals, when they built the tower
in the land of Assyria—and they were all of one speech,
and they wished to ascend into the starry heaven;
and immediately the Immortal imposed a great compulsion
upon the winds; and then the winds cast down the great tower from on high
and stirred up strife among mortals against one another;
therefore mortals gave the name Babylon to the city.
Then, when the tower fell and the tongues of men
were divided into all kinds of languages, and the whole
earth of mortals was filled with divided kingdoms,
then indeed was the tenth generation of articulate men,
ever since the Flood came upon earlier men.
And Cronus reigned, and Titan and Iapetus,
the most excellent children of Gaia and Ouranos, whom
men called Earth and Heaven, giving them the name,
because they were the very first of articulate men.
Three indeed were the portions of the earth according to each one's lot,
and each reigned holding his portion, and they did not fight;
for there were oaths to their father and righteous divisions.
Then the full time of the father's old age arrived,
and he died; and the sons, committing a terrible
transgression against their oaths, stirred up strife against one another,
as to who, holding the royal honor, should rule over all mortals;
and Cronus and Titan fought against each other.
Then Rhea and Gaia and garland-loving Aphrodite,
Demeter and Hestia and fair-tressed Dione,
brought them to friendship, having gathered together the kings,
all their brothers and kinsmen, and also other
men who were of their blood and parents;
and they judged that King Cronus should rule over all,
because he was the eldest and most excellent in form.
But Titan in turn imposed great oaths on Cronus,
not to rear male offspring, so that he himself might reign
when old age and fate should come upon Cronus.
Whenever Rhea gave birth, beside her sat
the Titans, and tore apart all the male children,
but the females they allowed to live, to be reared by their mother.
But when queenly Rhea gave birth the third time,
she bore Hera first; and when they saw with their eyes
a female infant, the wild Titan men departed
to their own. And then Rhea gave birth to a male child,
whom she quickly sent away secretly to be reared apart
in Phrygia, having chosen three Cretan men bound by oath;
therefore they named him Zeus, because he was sent away.
And in the very same way she secretly sent away Poseidon.
Third, in turn, Rhea, noble among women, bore Pluto
as she passed by Dodona, whence flowed the watery ways
of the river Europus, and its water poured down into the sea,
mingled with the Peneus, and they call it Stygian.
When the Titans heard that there were sons kept
in secret, whom Cronus had begotten with Rhea his consort,
Titan gathered together his sixty sons,
And he held in bonds Cronus and Rhea his consort,
and hid them in the earth and guarded them in fetters.
And then indeed the sons of mighty Cronus heard of it
and stirred up against him a great war and turmoil.
And this was the beginning of war for all mortals.
[For this was the very first beginning of war for mortals.]
And then God delivered disaster to the Titans.
And all the generations of the Titans and of Cronus
died. But thereafter, as time rolled on,
the kingdom of Egypt arose, then that of the Persians,
of the Medes and Ethiopians and Assyrian Babylon,
then of the Macedonians, again of Egypt, and then of Rome.
And then the utterance of the great God within my breast
arose and commanded me to prophesy throughout every
land, and to put into the minds of kings the things that are to be.
And this God first put into my mind,
how many kingdoms of mortals will be raised up.
For first of all the Solomonic house shall rule,
and Phoenicians, invaders of Asia and of other
islands, and the race of Pamphylians and Persians and Phrygians,
and of Carians and Mysians and the race of gold-rich Lydians.
And then the Greeks, arrogant and impure;
another great, manifold nation of Macedonia shall rule,
who will bring a fearful cloud of war upon mortals.
Yet the heavenly God will utterly destroy it from the depth.
And then there shall be the dominion of another kingdom,
white and many-headed, from the western sea,
which shall rule over much land and shake many people,
and thereafter cause fear for all kings,
and will plunder much gold and silver
from many cities; and again upon the divine earth there shall be
gold, and thereafter also silver and adornment.
And they will oppress mortals; but great shall be the fall
for those men, whenever they begin unjust arrogance.
And immediately among them there will be the constraint of impiety:
male will approach male, and they will place boys
in shameful brothels; and in those days there will be
great distress among mortals, and it will throw all things into confusion,
and shatter all things, and fill all things with evils
through vile greed for money and ill-gotten wealth,
in many lands, but especially in Macedonia.
And it will stir up hatred, and every deceit will be found among them,
[until the seventh kingdom, over which
a king of Egypt shall reign, who will be of Greek descent.]
And then the nation of the great God shall again be strong,
who will be guides of life to all mortals.
But why did God also put this into my mind to tell,
what evil will come first, what next, and what last
upon all mortals, and what will be the beginning of these things?
First God will bring disaster upon the Titans;
For they will pay penalties to the sons of mighty Cronus,
because indeed they bound Cronus and his honored mother.
Secondly, there will again be tyrannies among the Greeks, and haughty
kings, arrogant and impure,
adulterous and utterly evil; and no longer will there be for mortals
any cessation of war. And the terrible Phrygians will all perish,
and there will be evil for Troy on that day.
Immediately evil will also come upon the Persians and the Assyrians,
and all Egypt and Libya and the Ethiopians,
and against Carians and Pamphylians evil will be set in motion,
and upon all mortals. Why then do I declare each one in detail?
Yet whenever the first things reach an end, immediately there will be
the second upon humankind. And yet first of all I will cry aloud:
evil will come upon pious men who dwell around
the great Temple of Solomon, and who are descendants
of righteous men. In like manner I will cry aloud concerning
the tribe and generation of their fathers and the people of them all,
all things very clearly, O mortal of diverse wiles, deceitful of mind.
There is a city [...] on the earth, Ur of the Chaldeans,
from which comes a race of most righteous men,
who are always concerned with good counsel and noble deeds.
For neither the circular course of the sun nor that of the moon,
nor monstrous marvels upon the earth do they ponder,
nor the depth of the gray-eyed sea of Ocean,
nor signs of sneezes, nor the birds of augurs,
nor soothsayers, nor sorcerers, nor indeed charmers,
nor the deceitful foolish tales of ventriloquists,
nor do they cast horoscopes according to the divinations of the Chaldeans,
nor indeed do they practice astronomy; for all such things are by nature errors,
whatever foolish men search out day by day,
exercising their souls in no useful work;
and indeed they taught shameful errors to men,
from which many evils arise for mortals upon the earth,
in being led astray from good ways and righteous deeds.
Instead, they care for righteousness and virtue,
and not for love of money, which breeds countless evils
for mortal men: war and endless famine.
They maintain just measures both in fields and in cities,
nor do they commit night thefts against one another,
nor do they drive off herds of oxen and sheep and goats,
nor does neighbor remove the boundary markers of a neighbor's land,
nor does a very wealthy man distress the lesser,
nor does he oppress widows, but rather helps them,
always supplying them with grain, wine, and oil;
and always the prosperous man among the people sends to those who have nothing,
but are destitute, a portion of the harvest,
fulfilling the command of the great God, the lawful hymn;
for the Heavenly One made the earth common to all.
And when it leaves Egypt and journeys on the path,
the twelve-tribed people, under God-sent leaders,
marching by night in a pillar of fire,
and leading the way through all the day in a pillar of cloud,
and for this people he will appoint as leader a great man,
Moses, whom a princess found by the marsh and carried off,
and having reared him, called him her son. But when he came
leading this people, whom God brought out from Egypt
to Mount Sinai, then God from heaven beforehand
gave the Law, writing all righteous decrees on two tablets,
and commanded them to keep them; and if anyone should disobey,
he should pay the penalty either by law or at the hands of mortals,
or, if escaping the notice of mortals, he will perish by full justice.
For the Heavenly One made the earth common to all,
and gave faith and the best understanding within their breasts.
For them alone the life-giving earth produces fruit
a hundredfold from one, and the measures of God are fulfilled.
Yet indeed evil shall come even upon these, nor will they escape
the plague. And you especially, having abandoned the glorious temple,
shall flee, since it is your destiny to leave the holy soil.
You will be led away to the Assyrians, and you will see
your young children and wives serving as slaves among hostile men;
and all your livelihood and wealth will perish,
and every land and every sea will be filled with you,
and everyone will take offense at your customs.
All your land will become desolate, and the fortified altar
and the temple of the great God and the long walls
will all fall to the ground, because in your heart you did not obey
the holy law of the immortal God, but going astray,
you served shameful idols, and having no fear
of the immortal Father of all gods and mortals,
you refused to honor him, but honored the idols of mortals.
Because of these things, for seven decades of years the fruit-bearing land
will be completely desolate of you, and the wonders of the temple also.
Yet an outcome of good and the greatest glory awaits you,
even as the immortal God appointed for you. But you, remain steadfast,
trusting in the holy laws of the great God,
until he raises your weary knee upright toward the light.
And then indeed the heavenly God will send a king,
and he will judge each person in blood and the radiance of fire.
And there is a certain royal tribe, whose lineage will be
unfailing; and as times revolve, this lineage
will rule and begin to rebuild a new temple of God.
And all the kings of the Persians will furnish aid,
providing gold and bronze and much-wrought iron.
For God himself will send a holy vision by night,
and then indeed the temple will stand again, just as it was before.
When indeed my soul ceased from the inspired hymn,
and I entreated the great Father to release me from the constraint,
once again the word of the great God stirred within my breast,
stood and commanded me to prophesy throughout all
the earth, and to put things to come in the minds of kings.
And this did God first put into my mind to speak,
how many grievous woes the Immortal devised for Babylon,
because she sacked his great temple.
Woe to you, Babylon, and to the race of Assyrian men!
A rushing blast shall one day reach all the land of sinners,
and a battle cry shall destroy every land of mortal men,
and the stroke of the great God, the leader of hymns.
For through the air shall come upon you, Babylon, one day from above,
[nay, from heaven from the holy places shall descend upon you]
and upon the children of wrath an everlasting destruction.
And then you shall be as you were before, as though you had never existed;
and then you shall be filled with blood, just as formerly you yourself
poured out that of good men and righteous men,
whose blood even now cries out to the high ether.
A great stroke shall come to your houses, Egypt,
a terrible one, which you never expected would come upon you.
For a sword shall pass through the midst of you,
and scattering and death and famine shall hold sway
in the seventh generation of kings, and then you shall cease.
Woe to you, land of Gog and Magog, situated in the midst
of the rivers of Ethiopia; how great an outpouring of blood you shall receive,
and you shall be called among mortals the house of judgment,
and your dew-drenched earth shall drink dark blood.
Woe to you, Libya; and woe to both sea and land!
Daughters of the West, how you shall come to a bitter day!
You shall come pursued by a grievous struggle,
dreadful and hard; a terrible judgment shall take place again,
and of necessity you shall all go into destruction,
because you laid waste the great house of the Immortal
and chewed it terribly with iron teeth.
Therefore you shall indeed see your land full of corpses,
some by war and every demonic assault,
by famine and plague, and by barbarous foes.
And all your land shall be desolate, and your cities desolate.
And in the west a star will shine, which they will call a comet,
a sign to mortals of sword, famine, and death,
and destruction of leaders and of great, distinguished men.
And again there shall be very great signs among humankind;
for the deep-swirling Tanais shall leave Lake Maeotis,
and along the deep stream there shall be the course of a fruitful
furrow, and the countless current shall hold the neck of land.
There shall be chasms and yawning abysses; and many cities
shall fall with all their people: in Asia, Iassos,
Cebren, Pandonia, Colophon, Ephesus, Nicaea,
Antioch, Tanagra, Sinope, Smyrna, Maros,
most wealthy Gaza, Hierapolis, Astypalaea;
and of Europe, famous Cyagra, queenly Meropeia,
Antigone, Magnesia, all-divine Mycenae.
Know then that the destructive race of Egypt is near destruction,
and then for the Alexandrians the past year was better.
However much wealth Rome received from tribute-bearing Asia,
three times as much wealth shall Asia receive back
from Rome, and shall repay destructive insolence to her.
And as many as from Asia served the house of the Italians,
twenty times as many Italians shall serve as hirelings in Asia,
in poverty, and they shall owe ten-thousand-fold.
O luxurious, gold-laden Rome, offspring of the Latin land,
virgin, often drunken with your many-wooed marriages,
as a slave you shall be wed in no orderly manner,
and often a mistress will shear your delicate hair,
and administering justice from heaven down to earth
shall cast you, and from earth raise you up again to heaven,
because mortals were bound in a base and unjust life.
Samos also shall be sand, Delos shall be unseen,
and Rome a ruin; and all the divine oracles shall be fulfilled.
For Smyrna perishing there is no account; she shall be avenged,
yet through evil counsels and the wickedness of rulers—
and tranquil peace shall journey to the land of Asia;
and Europe shall then be blessed; a fertile climate,
long-lasting, robust, free of winter storms and free of hail,
bearing all things, both winged creatures and creeping beasts of the earth.
O blessed is the man who shall live until that time,
or woman—even as a field-dwelling peasant of the blessed;
for all good order from the starry heaven
shall come upon mortals, and righteous justice, and with it
prudent harmony, surpassing all things among mortals,
and affection, faith, and friendship from strangers and citizens alike;
and lawlessness, blame, envy, wrath, and folly
and poverty shall flee from humans; and necessity shall flee,
and murder, destructive strifes, and mournful quarrels,
and nocturnal thefts, and every evil in those days.
Yet Macedonia shall bring forth a grievous woe for Asia,
and for Europe the greatest sorrow shall sprout forth
from the line of Cronides, an offspring of bastards and slaves.
She shall also master fortified Babylon city,
and having been proclaimed mistress of every land that the sun looks upon,
she shall perish by evil ruin,
leaving a name among far-wandering posterity.
And at some time a faithless man shall come to the rich soil of Asia,
a man clad with a purple cloak upon his shoulders,
savage, foreign-judging, fiery; for a thunderbolt
raised him beforehand as a man of light; and all Asia shall bear an evil yoke,
and the earth, drenched, shall drink much slaughter.
Yet even so Hades shall attend to all into complete oblivion;
and of those whose race he himself wishes to destroy,
by their race shall his own race be destroyed,
leaving one root, which the man-destroyer shall also cut off
out of ten horns, and shall plant another shoot beside it.
He will cut down the warrior father of the purple race,
and he himself by his own sons in concerted fated strife
shall perish; and then indeed a side-sprouting horn shall rule.
And there shall also be a sign straightway for life-sustaining Phrygia,
whenever Rhea's defiled offspring, a continuous surge in the earth,
flourishing with unthirsting roots,
shall vanish root and branch in a single night
in a city destroyed with its people by the earth-shaking Earth-Shaker,
which one day they will call by the name Dorylaion
of ancient, much-lamented, dark Phrygia.
At that time then the one named Earth-Shaker
will break open the hollows of the earth and shatter walls.
And these are not signs of good, but the beginning of evil will arise.
It will have rulers skilled in all-tribal warfare,
giving forth native Aeneadae, kindred blood.
But afterward you shall be a prey for human lovers.
Ilion, I pity you; for throughout Sparta an Erinys
will sprout forth, a beautiful, ever-famed, noble shoot,
leaving behind a widespread surging wave for Asia and Europe;
and bringing above all to you wailing, toils, and groans,
she will establish them; but there will be ageless renown for future generations.
And there will arise in turn a certain lying-writing old mortal,
false to his fatherland; and the light will sink in his eyes;
and he will have a great mind and metrical speech fitted to his thoughts,
mingled under two names; and he will call himself
a Chian, and will write of the events concerning Ilion, not truly indeed,
but skillfully; for he will master my words and meters;
for he will be the first to unroll my books with his hands;
and he himself in turn will greatly adorn the armored warriors of battle,
Hector son of Priam and Achilles son of Peleus,
and the others who care for the works of war.
And indeed he will make the gods stand beside them,
writing falsehoods in every way for empty-headed mortals.
And wide renown shall belong rather to those who died
at Ilion; but he himself also shall receive deeds in return.
And the race of the Locrian will plant many evils for Lycia.
Chalcedon, holding the strait of the narrow sea,
an Aetolian youth coming will one day despoil you too.
Cyzicus, from you also the sea will tear away vast wealth.
And you, Byzantium, will once welcome war against Asia,
and indeed you will receive groans and uncounted bloodshed.
And high Mount Cragus in Lycia, from its peaks
through chasms of cleft rock water will gush forth murmuring,
until it puts an end to the oracular signs of Patara.
Cyzicus, dweller by the wine-dark Propontis,
the Rhyndacus surging in a wave around you will crash with a roar.
And you, Rhodes, will be unenslaved for a long time,
daughter of Day, and much wealth shall be yours thereafter,
and you will hold power upon the sea surpassing others.
But afterward you will be a prey to lustful men,
in beauties and in wealth; he will place a terrible yoke upon your neck.
Then a Lydian earthquake will ravage the things of Persia,
bringing to pass most chilling sorrows for Europe and Asia.
And the destructive king of the Sidonians and the battle-din of others
shall bring seafaring, destructive ruin upon the Samians.
The ground will murmur with the blood of dying men
flowing into the sea, and wives with splendidly robed daughters
will bewail their own shameful outrage,
some over the dead, and others over their perishing sons.
A sign for Cyprus: an earthquake will destroy the ravines,
and Hades will claim many souls together.
And Tralles, neighbor of Ephesus, will overthrow by earthquake
both well-built walls and the population of heavy-hearted men;
and the ground will rain down hot water, and back upon itself
the weighed-down earth will drink it; and there will be an odor of brimstone.
And Samos in due time will build royal palaces.
Italy, to you no foreign war will come,
but civil bloodshed, full of groaning and by no means weak,
widely spoken of and shameless, will ravage you.
And you yourself, stretched out beside hot ashes,
unforeseeing, will strike yourself down in your own breast.
You will not be a mother of good men, but a nurse of wild beasts.
But when a destroyer comes from Italy,
then, Laodicea, fallen headlong,
splendid city of the Carians by the wondrous water of the Lycus,
you will be silent, bewailing your boastful parent.
And the Thracian Crobyzi will rise up along Haemus.
For the Campanians there will be gnashing of teeth because of the fruitful
famine; and for many years [they will lament their parents].
Corsica and Sardinia, driven by great storm-blasts of winter
and by the blows of the holy God into the depths of the sea,
shall sink beneath the wave with their sea-born children.
Alas, how many maidens Hades will wed as brides,
and how many unburied youths the deep will tend;
alas for infant children swimming in the sea, and for heavy wealth!
Blessed land of the Mysians, a royal race suddenly
will arise. Truly, not for a long time will Carthage
endure; and for the Galatians there will be a lamentable pity.
An extreme and very great evil will come upon Tenedos as well.
And brazen Sicyon with loud shouts will boast over you,
Corinth, over all; and equally the flute will resound.
When indeed my spirit ceased from the inspired hymn,
again the utterance of the great God in my breast
stood up and commanded me to prophesy throughout the earth:
Alas for the race of Phoenicians, both men and women,
and for all coastal cities! Not one of you
will remain in the light of the sun in common daylight,
nor will there still be a remnant of the living or any tribe left,
because of an unjust tongue and a lawless, impure life,
which all spent in common, opening an impure mouth,
and they spoke dreadful, false, and unjust words,
and set themselves against God, the great King,
and deceitfully opened a vile mouth. Therefore,
may he terribly subdue them with plagues throughout all
the earth, and God will send a bitter fate upon them,
burning cities and many foundations from the ground.
Woe to you, Crete, full of sorrow! To you indeed shall come
a stroke, and fearful, eternal ruin shall lay you waste,
and all the earth will see you smoking again,
and fire will never leave you for ever, but you will be burned.
Woe to you, Thrace, how you will come under a slavish yoke,
when the mingled Galatians together with the Dardanidae
eagerly ravage Hellas—then evil will come upon you;
and to a foreign land you will give ... and receive nothing.
Woe to you, Gog, and to all together next in order, Magog,
Marsi and Angi, how many evils fate brings near to you,
[and many] also to the sons of the Lycians, Mysians, and Phrygians.
And many nations of the Pamphylians and Lydians will fall,
and of the Moors and Ethiopians, and of the barbarous-tongued nations,
and of the Cappadocians and Arabs. Why indeed do I utter each
in turn? For upon all who inhabit the earth,
the Most High will send a terrible stroke upon the nations.
And whenever a numerous barbarian nation attacks the Greeks,
it will destroy many heads of chosen men;
and they will ravage many fat sheep of mortals,
and herds of horses, mules, and loud-bellowing oxen;
and well-built houses they will lawlessly burn with fire;
and many captive persons they will forcibly lead away
to another land, both children and deep-girded women
from their bridal chambers, tender women who previously stepped on delicate feet;
they will see them in bonds under barbarous-tongued enemies,
suffering every terrible outrage; and there will not be for them
anyone to ward off war even a little, nor any helper of life.
And they will see their own possessions and all their wealth
reaped by an enemy; and trembling will be beneath their knees.
A hundred will flee, and one will destroy them all;
and five will arouse heavy wrath. And those against them,
shamefully thrown into turmoil in war and terrible uproar,
will bring joy to enemies, but mourning to the Greeks.
And indeed a slavish yoke will be upon all Hellas;
and together upon all mortals war and pestilence will come,
and God will make the great heaven above like bronze,
and drought over the whole earth, and the earth itself like iron.
Then thereafter all mortals will weep bitterly
over the failure to sow and lack of plowing; and fire on earth
will he lay down, he who created heaven and earth;
and only a third part of all mankind will remain thereafter.
O Hellas, why have you trusted in mortal men as leaders,
who are not able to escape the end of death?
And to what end do you offer vain gifts to the dead,
And do you sacrifice to idols? Who put such delusion in your mind
to perform these things, forsaking the face of the great God?
Revere the name of the All-Begetter, and let it not escape your mind.
A thousand years have passed, and five hundred more besides,
since haughty kings reigned
over the Greeks, who first introduced evils to mortals,
setting up many idols of perished, dead gods,
on account of which it was shown to you to think vain things.
But when the wrath of the great God comes upon you,
then indeed you will recognize the face of the great God.
And all the souls of men, groaning loudly,
raising their hands up toward the broad heaven,
will begin to call upon the Great King as their defender
and to seek who will be their deliverer from the great wrath.
Come now, learn this and lay it to heart,
what woes there shall be as the years revolve.
If Hellas makes sacrifice of cattle and loud-bellowing bulls
as whole burnt offerings to the temple of the great God,
you will escape ill-omened war and fear
and plague, and you will escape the yoke of slavery again.
Yet until then there will be a race of ungodly men,
until this destined day attains its end.
For you will by no means sacrifice to God until all things take place,
whatever things God alone will purpose—they shall not remain unfulfilled—
and a strong necessity is laid upon all things to be accomplished.
There shall be again a holy race of godly men,
who devote themselves to the counsels and the mind of the Most High,
who will glorify the temple of the great God
with libations and the fat of burnt offerings and sacred hecatombs,
with sacrifices of well-fed bulls and unblemished rams,
firstborn sheep and fat flocks of lambs,
holily offering whole burnt offerings upon the great altar.
Having obtained a portion in the righteousness of the law of the Most High,
they will dwell in happiness in cities and fertile fields,
themselves exalted by the Immortal as prophets,
and bringing great joy to all mortals.
For to them alone the great God gave wise counsel
and faith and an excellent understanding in their breasts;
who do not by empty delusions honor the works of men,
made of gold and bronze and silver and ivory,
and idols of wood and stone of departed dead gods,
clay figures smeared with red ochre, modelled images of animals,
all the things that mortals honor with vain-minded counsel.
Instead, they lift up holy arms toward heaven,
rising at dawn from bed, ever purifying their bodies
with water, and they honor only the one who reigns forever,
the Immortal, and next their parents; and exceedingly beyond all
men, they are mindful of a holy marriage bed;
nor do they have unchaste intercourse with male youths,
as do the Phoenicians, the Egyptians, and the Latins,
and spacious Hellas and many nations of others,
of Persians and Galatians and of all Asia, having transgressed
the holy law of immortal God, which they transgressed;
wherefore the Immortal will bring upon all mortals
ruin and famine and woes and groaning,
and war and plague and tearful sorrows;
because the immortal Begetter of all men
they would not honor holily, but honored idols,
worshiping handmade things, which mortals themselves will cast away,
hiding them in the clefts of the rocks for shame,
whenever a young king of Egypt, the seventh, rules
over his own land, reckoned from the Greeks'
dominion, which the boundless Macedonians shall rule;
and there shall come from Asia a great king, a gleaming eagle,
who will cover the whole earth with foot-soldiers and horsemen,
and cut everything to pieces and fill all things with evils;
and he will overthrow the kingdom of Egypt; and having seized all
its possessions, he will ride upon the broad back of the sea.
And then indeed they shall bend to the great God, the King,
the Immortal, the white knee upon the all-nourishing earth;
and all handmade works will fall into the flame of fire.
And then indeed God will give great joy to men;
for the earth and trees and boundless flocks of sheep
will give their true fruit to mortals,
of wine and sweet honey and white milk
and wheat, which is the finest of all things for mortals.
But do not linger, O mortal of cunning counsel, nor delay,
but turn back from wandering and propitiate God.
Sacrifice to God hecatombs of bulls and lambs,
firstlings, and goats, as the seasons revolve.
Propitiate him, the immortal God, if perchance he may have mercy;
for he alone is God, and there is no other.
And honor righteousness, and oppress no one;
for these things the Immortal commands wretched mortals.
Beware the wrath of the great God,
whenever the end of the plague comes upon all mortals
and they, vanquished, meet fearful judgment,
and king captures king and takes away his land,
and nations ravage nations and rulers destroy peoples,
and all the commanders flee into another land,
and the land of mortals is altered, and a barbarian empire
ravages all Hellas and drains the fertile land
of its wealth, and they enter into strife against one another
on account of gold and silver; love of money
will shepherd evils for the cities—
in a foreign land, and all shall be unburied,
and vultures and wild beasts of the earth
shall devour their flesh; and when these things are fulfilled,
the monstrous earth will consume the remains of the dead.
And it shall all remain unsown and unplowed,
proclaiming, wretched one, the defilement of countless people.
through long lengths of time as the years revolve,
bucklers and large shields, javelins and variegated armor;
nor indeed will wood be cut from the thicket to kindle the blaze of fire.
And then from the sun God will send a king,
who will put an end to evil war across the whole earth,
slaying some, and fulfilling faithful treaties with others.
Nor indeed will he do all these things by his own counsels,
but obeying the noble decrees of the great God.
And again the temple of the great God, laden with exceedingly fair wealth,
with gold and silver and purple ornament;
and the earth will be fruit-bearing, and the sea
teeming with good things. And kings will begin
to be angry with one another, harboring malice in their heart;
envy is not a good thing for wretched mortals.
But again kings of the nations against this very land
will rush in a throng, bringing doom upon themselves;
for they will desire to plunder the sanctuary of the great God
and the finest men, whenever they reach the land.
The polluted kings will set their thrones around the city,
each having his throne and his disobedient people there.
And then God will speak with a great voice to all
the undisciplined, empty-minded people, and judgment upon them
will come from the great God, and all will perish
by the immortal hand; and from heaven will fall
fiery swords down upon the earth; torches, great flashing rays
will come, blazing into the midst of men.
And the earth, mother of all, will be shaken in those days
by the immortal hand, and the fish throughout the sea
and all the wild beasts of the earth and the countless tribes of winged birds
and all the souls of men and every sea
will shudder before the immortal face, and dread will be upon them.
And steep peaks of mountains and giant hills
he will shatter, and dark gloom will appear to all.
And misty ravines in the high mountains
will be full of corpses; and the rocks will flow
with blood, and every torrent will fill the plain.
And all the well-built walls of hostile men
will fall to the ground, because they did not know the Law
nor the judgment of the great God, but with senseless mind
you all rushed forth against the Temple, raising spears.
And God will judge all with war and with sword,
and with fire and deluge of rain; and there will be
brimstone from heaven, and stones and hail
plentiful and grievous; and death will come upon four-footed beasts.
And then they will acknowledge the immortal God, who judges these things;
and wailing and battle-cries throughout the boundless earth
will arise from perishing men; and all the defiled
will bathe in blood; and the earth itself will drink
the blood of the slain, and wild beasts will gorge on flesh.
The great and eternal God himself told me
to prophesy all these things; and these things will not remain unfulfilled,
nor unaccomplished, whatever he merely puts into his mind;
for the Spirit of God is without falsehood throughout the world.
And all the sons of the great God around the temple
shall live quietly, rejoicing in these things
which the Creator, the righteous Judge and Monarch, will give.
For he alone will shelter them, standing by them in majesty,
as though having a wall of burning fire all around them.
And they shall be free from war in cities and in the countryside.
For there will be no hand of evil war, but rather for them
the Immortal Himself and the hand of the Holy One shall be a defender.
And then indeed all islands and cities will say
how much the Immortal loves those men;
for all things fight alongside them and help them,
heaven, and the divinely driven sun, and the moon.
And from their mouths they will utter a sweet word in hymns:
"Come, let us all fall upon the earth and beseech
the immortal King, the great and eternal God.
Let us send to the temple, since he alone is the Sovereign;
and let us all ponder the law of the Most High God,
and the all-bearing earth will be shaken in those days,
which is the most righteous of all throughout the earth.
For we had wandered from the path of the Immortal,
and with foolish mind we revered handmade works,
idols and carved images of dead men."
These things the souls of faithful people will cry out:
["Come, falling on our faces among the people of God,
let us delight God the Begetter with hymns throughout our houses,
procuring the weapons of the enemies throughout the whole earth
for the duration of seven revolving years—
light shields and oblong shields, helmets and all kinds of armor,
and many things and a multitude of bows and unjust missiles;
for no wood will be cut from the forest for the light of fire."]
But, wretched Hellas, cease thinking proud thoughts;
beseech the great-hearted Immortal and be on your guard;
do not dispatch your ill-advised people against this city,
which is not from the holy land of the Great One.
Do not move Camarina—for it is better unmoved—
nor a leopard from its lair, lest evil meet you;
but keep away, and do not hold in your breast an arrogant,
overweening spirit, sending [them] to a mighty contest.
And serve the great God, so that you may share in these things.
And whenever that fated day reaches its end,
[and judgment of the immortal God shall come upon mortals,]
great judgment and dominion will come upon humankind.
For the all-bearing earth will give to mortals the best,
boundless fruit of grain, wine, and olive oil,
[and from heaven a sweet drink of luscious honey,
and trees [will yield] the fruit of tree-nuts and fat sheep,]
and cattle, and lambs from sheep, and kids from goats;]
and it will burst forth sweet springs of white milk;
and cities in turn will be full of good things, and the fields
will be fertile; nor will there be a sword across the earth, nor battle-din;
nor will the earth shake any longer, groaning heavily;
no war, nor again drought across the earth will there be any more,
no famine, nor hail that destroys the harvest;
but indeed there will be great peace throughout all the earth,
and king will be friend to king until the end
of the age, and a common law throughout all the earth
the Immortal One in starry heaven will establish for humankind,
for all that has been done by wretched mortals.
For he alone is God, and there is no other;
he himself will also consume with fire the race of harsh men.
Instead, make haste in your minds within your breasts,
flee lawless worship, serve the living One;
guard against adultery and indiscriminate bed with males;
raise your own offspring of children and do not murder them;
for at these things the Immortal One will be angered, against whoever sins.
And then indeed he will raise up a kingdom for all ages
over all people, he who once gave the holy law
to the pious, to all of whom he promised to open the earth
and the world, and the gates of the blessed, and all joys,
and immortal understanding and eternal gladness.
And from every land they will bring frankincense and gifts to the house
of the great God; and there will be no other
house for people to learn of, even in generations to come,
except the one God gave to faithful people to honor.
[For mortals will call him the son of the great God,]
And all paths of the plain and rough ridges,
towering mountains and wild waves of the sea,
will become easy to traverse and easy to sail in those days;
for every peace of good things comes upon the earth;
and the prophets of the great God will take away the sword;
for they themselves are judges of mortals and righteous kings.
There will indeed also be righteous wealth among people;
for this is the judgment and also the rule of the great God.
Rejoice, maiden, and be glad; for to you he has given
eternal gladness, he who created heaven and earth.
And he will dwell in you; and to you he will be an immortal light;
and wolves and lambs together will feed on grass in the mountains,
and leopards will graze together with young goats;
wandering bears will lodge together with calves;
and the flesh-eating lion will eat straw at the manger
like an ox; and very young children will lead them
in leashes; for he will make the wild beast tame upon the earth.
And serpents will sleep with infants alongside asps
and will do no harm; for the hand of God will be upon them.
And I will tell you a very clear sign, so that you may perceive
when indeed the end of all things comes upon earth.
When swords are seen in the starry sky
by night toward the west and toward the east,
and immediately dust is borne down from heaven
upon the whole earth, and the brilliance of the sun
shall fail from the midst of heaven, and the moon's
rays shall shine forth and return again to the earth;
and a sign shall come from the rocks with drops of blood;
and in a cloud you shall see a battle of infantry and cavalry,
like a hunt of wild beasts, resembling mists.
God who dwells in heaven shall bring about this end of war.
But all must sacrifice to the Great King.
These things to you, having left the long Babylonian walls of Assyria,
in a frenzy of inspiration, predicting fire sent against Greece,
prophesying the wrath of God to all mortals—
so that I prophesy divine riddles to mortals.
And mortals throughout Greece will call me from another fatherland,
a shameless woman born of Erythrae; and some will say that I am the Sibyl
born of mother Circe and father Gnostos,
a raving liar; but when all things come to pass,
then you will remember me, and no longer will anyone
call me mad, the prophetess of the great God.
For he did not reveal to me the things that were before to my parents;
but whatever things happened first, these God recounted to me,
and all things thereafter God placed in my mind,
so that I might prophesy both things to come and things that were before,
and speak them to mortals. For when the world was inundated
with waters, and a certain approved man alone was left,
having sailed on the waters in a wooden house
together with beasts and birds, so that the world might be filled again;
of him I was a daughter-in-law, and from his blood I came,
to whom the first events occurred; and the last things have all been shown;
so let all these true things be spoken from my mouth.
Fourth Book
Hear, people of boastful Asia and Europe,
all the utterly true things that through the honey-voiced mouth
of our shrine I am about to prophesy;
no oracle-singer of false Phoebus, whom foolish
men called a god, and falsely proclaimed a prophet;
but of the Great God, whom the hands of men did not fashion
like mute idols carved from stone.
For he does not have as a house a stone dragged into a temple,
utterly deaf and senseless, a grievous outrage to mortals;
but one who cannot be seen from the earth or measured
by mortal eyes, not having been fashioned by mortal hand;
who, looking down upon all at once, is himself seen by no one;
whose are dark night and day and the sun,
the stars and the moon and the fish-bearing sea,
and the earth and the rivers and the mouth of ever-flowing springs,
creations for life, and rains producing both the fruit of the field
and trees, the grapevine, and the olive tree.
He drove a whip inward through my heart,
to tell mortals all that is now and all that will be hereafter,
reaching from the first generation unto the tenth,
to recount accurately; for he himself will test all things
as he fulfills them. But do you, O people, listen in all things to the Sibyl,
pouring forth true speech from a holy mouth.
Blessed among mortals upon the earth shall those be
who will love the great God, blessing him
before drinking and eating, trusting in piety;
who will reject all temples when they see them,
and altars, pointless foundations of dumb stones,
and stone images and handmade statues,
defiled with the blood of animate beings and sacrifices
of quadrupeds; but they will look to the great glory of the one God,
neither committing reckless murder nor trafficking in
stolen gain, which are the most dreadful things,
nor having shameful desire for another's bed,
[nor hateful and abominable outrage with a male].
Whose way, piety, and customs other men
will never imitate, desiring shamelessness;
instead, sneering at them with mockery and laughter,
fools in their senselessness will falsely accuse them
of whatever reckless and evil deeds they themselves commit.
For the entire race of mortal men is hard of belief. But when at last
the judgment of the world and of mortals comes, which God himself
will execute, judging the ungodly and the pious together;
and then he will send the impious under the gloom into fire,
[and then they will realize how great an impiety they committed];
but the pious will remain upon the grain-giving land,
when God gives spirit and life and grace together to them.
All these things will be fully accomplished in the tenth generation;
and now all that will happen from the first generation, these things I will speak.
First the Assyrians will rule over all mortals,
holding dominion over the world in their rule for six generations,
from the time when, because the heavenly God was wrathful,
together with cities themselves and all mortals,
the sea covered the earth when the flood burst forth.
Overthrowing them, the Medes will boast upon the thrones,
for whom there will be only two generations, during which these deeds will happen:
there will be dark night at the middle hour of day;
and the stars will fail from heaven, and the disks of the moon;
and the earth, shaken by the turmoil of a great earthquake,
will cast headlong many cities and the works of men;
and then islands will emerge from the depths of the sea.
But when the great Euphrates overflows with blood,
even then a dread battle-strife between Medes and Persians
will arise in war; and falling beneath the spears of the Persians, the Medes
will flee across the great water of the Tigris.
And the power of the Persians will be greatest over the whole world,
for whom one generation is appointed of prosperous royal rule.
And there will be evil deeds, as many as men pray to avert:
battles and slaughters, dissensions and flights,
the overthrow of towers and the ruin of cities,
when boastful Hellas sails over the broad Hellespont,
bringing grievous doom to the Phrygians and to Asia.
Moreover, into Egypt, rich in furrows and wheat-bearing,
famine and barrenness shall come as twenty revolving years
run their course, when the ear-nurturing Nile
shall hide its dark water somewhere else beneath the earth.
And a king shall come from Asia raising a great spear,
with unnumbered ships; he shall tread on foot the wet paths of the deep
and shall sail cutting through the high-crested mountain;
cowardly Asia shall receive him back as a fugitive from war.
And all wretched Sicily shall be utterly consumed
by a stream of great fire, as Etna belches forth flame;
and Croton, a great city, shall fall into a deep stream.
And there will be strife in Hellas; raging against one another,
they will cast down many cities and destroy many
in their fighting; and the strife will be evenly matched among them.
But when the race of mortal men comes to the tenth generation,
then there shall be a yoke of slavery and fear for the Persians.
Then when the Macedonians boast of their royal scepters,
afterward there shall also be an evil capture for Thebes,
and Carians shall dwell in Tyre, while the Tyrians shall perish.
And sand shall cover all Samos beneath the shores,
and Delos shall no longer be visible, and all that is of Delos shall become unseen.
And Babylon, great to look upon but small in fighting,
shall stand, fortified on useless hopes.
Macedonians shall settle Bactra, but those from Bactra
and Susa shall all flee into the land of Hellas.
It will come to pass for future generations, when silver-eddying Pyramus,
pouring forth silt upon the shore, shall reach the sacred island.
And you, Baris, shall fall, and Cyzicus, when the earth
is shaken by earthquakes and cities slide into ruin.
Upon the Rhodians too shall come an evil, the last, but the greatest.
Nor shall the power of Macedonia endure; but from the west
a great Italian war shall blossom, under which the world
shall serve, bearing a slavish yoke for the daughters of Italy.
And you, wretched Corinth, shall one day look upon your own capture.
Carthage, your tower too shall bend its knee to the ground.
Wretched Laodicea, an earthquake will one day lay you low,
casting you down; yet you shall stand again, a city reestablished.
O fair Myra of Lycia, the shaken earth will never
support you; falling headlong down upon the ground
you will pray to flee as a resident alien to another land,
when on account of impieties the black water of the sea
shall spread over the tumult of Patara with thunders and earthquakes.
Armenia, a slavish constraint awaits you as well;
and upon Solyma too shall come an evil storm of war
from Italy, and it shall sack the great temple of God,
when, trusting in follies, piety indeed
they cast away, and perform hateful murders before the temple;
and then from Italy a great king, like a runaway slave,
will flee unseen, unheard of, across the passage of the Euphrates,
when indeed the maternal pollution of hateful murder
he will endure, and many other things, having yielded to an evil hand.
And many around the throne will bloody the soil of Rome,
when that one has fled away into the Parthian land.
And to Syria shall come a leader of Rome, who, with fire the temple
of Jerusalem having burned down, and having slain many men at once,
will destroy the great, wide-streeted land of the Jews.
And then indeed an earthquake will destroy both Salamis and Paphos,
when dark water overwhelms wave-washed Cyprus.
But whenever from an earthly fissure of the Italian land
a firebrand turned upward reaches the broad heaven,
and burns many cities and destroys men,
and much glowing ash fills the great sky,
and drops fall from heaven like red ochre,
know then the wrath of the heavenly God,
because they will destroy the guiltless race of the pious.
And to the west then the strife of awakening war
will come, and Rome's fugitive, raising a great spear,
having crossed the Euphrates with many tens of thousands.
Wretched Antioch, they shall never call you a city,
when through your follies you fall beneath spears.
And Cyrrhus then pestilence and dread battle will destroy.
Alas, miserable Cyprus, you the broad wave of the sea
will conceal, tossed by wintry blasts.
And to Asia shall come great wealth, which once Rome
herself, having plundered, in her house of many possessions
laid up; and then twice as much and more she will pay back
to Asia, and then there will be an excess of war's plunder.
And the cities of the Carians beside the waters of the Maeander,
as many as are built with beautiful towers, bitter famine
will destroy, when the Maeander hides its dark water.
But when faith in piety perishes from mortals,
and justice is hidden in the world,
... fickle ... and in unholy daring deeds
living, they commit outrage, reckless and evil deeds,
and no one takes account of the pious, but even them
all, through folly, utterly foolish ones destroy,
rejoicing in outrages and keeping their hands stained with blood;
and then know that God is no longer gentle,
but gnashing with anger and utterly destroying the race
of mortals all together by a great conflagration.
Ah, wretched mortals, change these things, and do not to wrath
of every kind provoke the great God, but casting aside
swords and groans, and homicides and outrages,
wash your whole bodies in ever-flowing rivers,
and stretching out your hands to heaven, for your former deeds
Ask for forgiveness, and with blessings propitiate
bitter impiety; God will grant repentance
and will not destroy; and he will stay his wrath again, if all of you
practice precious piety in your hearts.
But if you do not obey me, evil-minded ones, but loving
impiety, you receive all these things with evil ears,
there will be fire over the whole world and a very great sign
with sword and trumpet at the rising of the sun;
the whole world will hear a roaring and a mighty noise.
And it will burn the whole earth, and destroy the entire race of men,
and all cities, and rivers together with the sea;
and it will burn everything up, and all will be smoldering dust.
But when already all things have become ashen dust,
and God puts to rest the boundless fire, just as he kindled it,
God himself will again fashion the bones and ash
of mortals, and raise humanity up again, as they were before.
And then indeed there will be a judgment, in which God himself will judge,
judging the world again; and as many as sinned through impieties,
these again the heaped-up earth will cover,
and moldy Tartarus and the gloomy recesses of Gehenna.
But as many as are pious shall live again upon the earth,
the immortal, great God giving imperishable prosperity
and the spirit of God, together with life and grace, to them,
to the pious; and then all will look upon one another,
beholding the sweet, delightful light of the sun.
O most blessed the man who will live to that time!
Fifth Book.
Come now, hear from me the lamentable time of the Latins.
Truly, first of all, after the kings who perished
of Egypt, all of whom the impartial earth received,
and after the founder of Pella, under whom all
the East was conquered, and the wealthy West,
whom Babylon exposed, and handed over as a corpse to Philip,
though he was proclaimed—not truly—to be of Zeus or Ammon,
and after the one of the race and blood of Assaracus,
who came from Troy, who cleaved the rushing fire,
and after many kings, after warlike men,
and after the infants, children of the sheep-devouring beast,
there will be a first king, who will reach the sum of twice ten
with his initial letter; and he will prevail greatly in wars;
and he will have the first mark from the tens; so that after him
he will rule who obtained the first letter of the alphabet as his initial;
before whom Thrace will cower, and Sicily, and next Memphis—
Memphis cast down prostrate through the wickedness of its rulers
and of an unsubdued woman who fell upon the wave.
And he will establish laws for the peoples and subject all things;
and after a long time he will hand over the rule to another,
who will have as his first letter the number three hundred
and the beloved name of a river; and over the Persians
he will rule, and Babylon; and then he will strike the Medes with the spear.
Then he who obtained the stroke of the number three will rule.
And he who will rule afterwards will have twice ten, as king
upon the first stroke; and he will reach
the farthest water of Ocean, darting on an ebb tide for the Ausonians.
And he who obtained the stroke of fifty will be sovereign,
a terrible serpent breathing out grievous war, who will one day stretch out his hands
against his own kin and destroy them, and throw all things into confusion,
competing in games, driving chariots, murdering, and daring countless atrocities;
and he will cut through the mountain between two seas and defile it with gore;
yet the destructive one will also vanish; then he will return,
making himself equal to God; but he will prove that he is not.
And after him three kings will perish by one another's hands.
Then a great destroyer of pious men will come,
who plainly displays the stroke of seven times ten.
And his son, who has the first stroke of three hundred, convicting him,
will strip away his power; and after him there will be a sovereign
from the stroke of four, of an ill-fated doom; but afterwards
a venerable mortal of the number fifty. But after him,
he who obtained the stamped beginning of the stroke of three hundred,
a mountain-walking Celt; and hastening toward the eastern conflict,
he will not escape an unseemly fate, but will perish;
whom foreign dust will hide as a corpse, yet dust bearing the name
of the flower of Nemea; and after him another will reign,
a silver-headed man; and he will have the name of a sea;
he will be an all-excellent man and will understand all things.
And in your time, all-excellent, most preeminent, dark-haired one,
and under your branches these days will endure through all time.
After him three will rule, and the third will hold sway late.
I, thrice-wretched, am exhausted to place an evil utterance in my heart,
the companion of Isis, and the inspired hymn of oracles.
First, around the foundation of your much-lamented temple
maenads will rush, and in wicked hands
you will be on that day, whenever the Nile travels over
the whole land of Egypt up to sixteen cubits,
so as to inundate all the earth and water it with its streams;
and the charm of the land and the glory of its appearance will be silenced.
Memphis, you indeed will weep most greatly for Egypt;
for you, who formerly held mighty sway over the land, will become
wretched, so that the Thunderer himself will cry aloud
from heaven with a loud voice: 'Mighty Memphis,
who of old boasted most greatly among wretched mortals,
you will weep, grievously distressed and all-ill-fated, so as to recognize
the eternal, immortal God himself in the clouds.
Where is the mighty pride that was fashioned for you among mortals?
Because you raged furiously against my anointed children
and incited wickedness against the righteous men,
you will have such a nurse in retribution for so many deeds.
No longer will there visibly be any divine right for you among the blessed;
you have fallen from the stars, you will not ascend into heaven.'
These things God bade to be proclaimed against Egypt,
in the last time, when men will be utterly evil.
Yet the wicked suffer wretchedly, awaiting the evil reward,
the wrath of the immortal, loud-thundering Heavenly One,
and worshiping stones and wild beasts instead of God,
fearing exceedingly many different things hither and thither, which have no reason,
no mind, no hearing—things not even lawful for me to speak of—
each of the idols, made by the hands of mortals.
And out of their own toils and reckless inventions
men accepted gods of wood and of stone,
and of bronze and gold and silver, vain,
lifeless, deaf, and smelted in fire;
they made them in vain, putting their trust in such things.
Thmuis and Xois are afflicted and stricken by the counsel
of Herakles, and of Zeus, and of Hermes.
And you too, Alexandria, famed nurse of cities,
war will not leave you, nor . . .
you will pay for your arrogance, for all that you did before.
You will be silent for a long age, and the day of return—
and no longer will a luxurious drink flow for you . . .
For a Persian will come upon your soil like hail,
and he will destroy your land and deceitful people,
with blood and corpses beside dreadful altars,
a savage-minded, mighty, bloody man, raging madly,
rushing with a sand-like multitude to your destruction.
And then, city of great wealth, you will have suffered much.
All Asia will weep for the sake of the gifts from you,
with which she crowned her head and rejoiced, falling upon the ground.
And he who received the land of the Persians will make war,
and killing every man he will ravage their whole livelihood,
so that a third portion remains for wretched mortals.
And he himself will fly in from the west with a light leap,
besieging the whole earth, laying all desolate.
But when he possesses mighty height and dreadful daring,
he will come wanting also to sack the city of the blessed.
And then a king sent from God against him
will destroy all the great kings and noble men.
Then thus will judgment come upon mortals by the Immortal One.
Alas for you, wretched heart! Why do you incite me
to declare these things to Egypt, a grievous rule of many?
Go toward the east, to the senseless race of the Persians,
and declare to them the present and what is about to be.
The stream of the river Euphrates will bring a flood,
and will destroy Persians and Iberians and Babylonians,
and the Massagetae who love war and trust in their bows.
All Asia, consumed by fire, will blaze as far as the islands.
Pergamum, once venerable, will perish in clusters,
and Pitane will appear utterly desolate among mortals.
All Lesbos will sink into the deep abyss so as to be destroyed.
Smyrna, rolling down the crags, will one day weep;
she who was once venerable and renowned will perish utterly.
Bithynians will weep for their land turned to ash,
and great Syria and populous Phoenicia.
Alas for you, Lycia, how many evils the sea devises against you,
assaulting of its own accord upon the woeful land,
so as to submerge with an evil earthquake and bitter waters
the dry land of Lycia, unperfumed, which was once sweet-scented.
There shall also be terrible wrath for Phrygia because of grief,
on account of which Rhea, daughter of Zeus, came and remained there.
The sea will destroy the race of the Tauri and the barbarian nation;
and it will strike down the Lapiths to the ground.
A river of deep eddies will destroy the Thessalian land,
Peneus of deep streams, sweeping the shapes of wild beasts from the earth,
Epidanus claiming that it once brought forth forms of wild beasts.
Poets will bewail thrice-wretched Hellas,
when from Italy one strikes the tendon of the isthmus,
the great king of great Rome, a godlike man,
whom, they say, Zeus himself and queenly Hera begot;
who, with all-musical voice singing honey-sweet hymns
while applauding in theaters, will destroy many along with his wretched mother.
A fearful and shameless ruler will flee from Babylon,
whom all mortals and noble men abhor;
for he destroyed many and laid hands upon the womb,
he sinned against wives, and was sprung from defiled folk.
And he will come to the Medes and to the kings of the Persians,
whom he first desired and upon whom he bestowed renown,
lurking with these evil men against the true nation;
who seized the divinely built temple and burned the citizens,
the people entering it, whom I have justly praised in song;
for when he appeared, the whole creation was shaken,
and kings perished, and among those in whom rule remained,
they destroyed both the great city and the righteous people.
But when a great star shines forth from the fourth year,
which alone will bring down the whole earth for the sake of honor,
which they first dedicated to marine Poseidon,
a great star will come from heaven into the divine sea
and burn the deep sea and Babylon itself
and the land of Italy, on whose account many perished,
holy, faithful Hebrews and the true people.
You shall suffer evils among mortal evils,
but you will remain utterly desolate for all ages hereafter,
[it shall be, but it will remain utterly desolate forever,]
hating your own soil, because you yearned for sorcery;
adulteries are found with you and unlawful union with boys,
effeminate and unjust, evil city, most ill-fated of all.
Alas, utterly unclean city of the Latin land,
frenzied Maenad rejoicing in vipers, you shall sit as a widow beside the banks,
and the river Tiber will weep for you, his consort,
you who have a bloodthirsty heart and an impious mind.
Did you not know what God can do, and what he devises?
Rather, you said: 'I am alone, and no one will sack me.'
Now the ever-existing God will destroy you and all yours,
and no longer will there be any sign of you in that land,
as of old, when the great God found your honors.
Remain alone, lawless one, and mingled with blazing fire,
inhabit the Tartarean, lawless realm in Hades.
And now again, Egypt, I lament your ruin:
Memphis, you will be the leader in troubles, smitten in your sinews;
in you the pyramids will utter a shameless voice.
Python, which of old was justly called the twin city,
be silent forever, so that you may cease from wickedness.
Insolence, treasury of evil troubles, much-lamenting maenad,
dire-suffering, full of tears, you will remain a widow forever.
For many years you alone were ruling the world.
But when Barke puts on the tunic
of white over the filthy, may I neither exist nor come to be.
O Thebes, where is your great strength? A savage man
will destroy the people; and you, having put on dark garments,
will lament alone, wretched one, and will pay for everything,
whatever you did before, having a shameless soul.
And they will see wailing because of lawless deeds.
And may a great man of the Ethiopians destroy Syene;
dark-skinned Indians will inhabit Teucheira by force.
Pentapolis, you will weep; and a man of great might will destroy you.
Who will recount your ruins, all-weeping Libya?
And who among mortals will weep piteously for you, Cyrene?
You will not cease from hateful lamentation until the time of destruction.
There will be among the Brygi and among the Gauls rich in gold
a roaring ocean filled with much blood;
for they themselves worked evil against the children of God,
when a Phoenician king led for the Sidonians a great Gallic
multitude out of Syria; and he will slaughter you,
even you, Ravenna, and will lead you to slaughter.
Do not be confident, Indians and high-spirited Ethiopians;
for when the wheel of the Pole-Axis, Capricorn,
and Taurus in Gemini encircle the mid-heaven,
and Virgo ascending, and the Sun fastening around his forehead
the all-encompassing belt, exercises sway,
there will be a great heavenly conflagration over the earth,
and a new nature among the warring stars, so that
the whole land of the Ethiopians will perish in fire and groanings.
Mourn also, Corinth, the mournful ruin within you;
for when the three sister Fates, spinning with twisted threads,
shall lead aloft him who fled by deceit beside the ridge of the Isthmus,
until all behold him,
the one who once cut through the rock with forged bronze;
and he will destroy and cut down your land, as has been ordained.
For God gave him power to do
such things as no one of all the previous kings ever did;
first, tearing up the roots from three heads with a blow,
and having greatly established it, he would give it to others to partake of,
so that they eat the flesh of the parents of the impure king.
For murder and terrors lie in store for all humankind
on account of the great city and the righteous people
which is preserved forever, which Providence held preeminent.
Unstable and ill-counseled one, encompassed by evil dooms,
beginning of toil and great end for humankind,
of creation harmed and again preserved by the Fates,
insolence, originator of evils and great bane to mortals,
who among mortals longed for you? Who was not grieved within?
In you a certain king perished, cast down from a revered life.
You arranged all things evilly and inundated all with evil,
and through you the fair folds of the cosmos were changed.
Perhaps you cast these last things forth into our strife:
How and what do you say? I will persuade you, and whatever I blame you for, I speak:
There was once among mortals a bright splendor of the sun,
a sown beam sharing the covenant of the prophets;
a tongue dripping honey, a noble drink for all mortals,
it shone forth and brought forth and caused gentle things to rise for all.
For this reason, narrow-minded originator of greatest evils,
both sword and mourning shall come on that day.
Beginning of toil and great end for humankind,
of creation harmed and again preserved by the Fates,
hear the bitter, ill-sounding report, you bane to men.
But whenever the Persian land desists from war,
from pestilence, and from groaning, then on that day shall be
the divine and heavenly race of the blessed Judeans,
who dwell around the city of God in the interior;
and having encircled a great wall as far as Joppa,
they are lifted high, even up to the dark clouds.
No longer will the trumpet pipe its war-clamoring sound,
nor will they perish any longer by hostile, raging hands,
but he will set up trophies over evils for all eternity.
And there will come again from heaven a certain preeminent man,
who stretched out his hands upon the fruitful tree,
the best of the Hebrews, who will one day stop the sun,
having called out with a noble utterance and pure lips.
No longer distress the soul within your breast, blessed one,
divine-born, all-wealthy, only-longed-for flower,
good light and revered end, pure longed-for object,
graceful Judea, beautiful city, inspired with hymns.
No longer will the unclean foot of the Greeks
revel throughout your land, bearing a lawless mind in their breasts;
but glorious children will honor you around,
and with holy music they will set the table
with sacrifices of every kind and with prayers honoring God.
As many as endured toils out of meager affliction,
the righteous will rule over greater, charming, and noble things;
while the wicked, having sent an unlawful tongue up toward the sky,
will cease speaking against one another,
and will hide themselves until the cosmos is transformed.
And there shall be a shower of blazing fire from the clouds;
